answer.reason: The verses tell a single chief event: Jael received the fleeing Sisera into her tent and killed him with a tent nail, which the summary names only as a relation.

clauses.english: took Sisera into her tent and killed him by driving a tent nail into his temples as he slept
clauses.quote: smote the nail into his temples, and fastened it into the ground

clauses.english: was blessed above women in the tent
clauses.quote: Blessed above women shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be

doubts: JDG 5:6 names Jael only to date the days of Shamgar, so it was left out.
The summary already names her as killer of Sisera, so the deed is told once as it happened.
